subtitle.text: Daisy: Jenna, it's finally here!
Jenna: Yay! Look, Daisy, I got a new backpack.
Daisy: Cool. I'm using my sister's old one.
Daisy: But that's okay.
I like frogs.
Jenna: I can't wait to go back to South Street School.
Jenna: And meet our teacher, Miss Gray.
Jenna: It's such a nice name.
Jenna: It rhymes with day, play, May . . . all great words!
Daisy: My sister said Miss Gray is really nice—and really pretty.
Jenna: I bet she lets us sit next to each other!
Jenna: Come on! Let's run!
Mark: Ugh! It's the first day of school, Coby!
Coby: Don't remind me.
Mark: What's our teacher's name?
I keep forgetting.
Coby: And I keep telling you, Mark!
It's Miss Gray.
Mark: Oh, right. Gray, like a gloomy rain cloud.
Coby: Or a big, creepy spider!
Mark: Yuck! Second grade is going to be awful!
Coby: So who's your teacher, Jenna?
Jenna: Miss Gray.
Daisy: She's really nice and really pretty.
Mark: That's not what we heard.
Mark: We heard she’s strange.
Coby: Yep. And she looks like an alien to me.
Jenna: What?
Mr. Joe: Welcome back, everyone.
Mr. Joe: It's time to line up with your class.
Daisy: You two are lying.
Mark: Nope. We only tell the truth.
Jenna: Really? She looks like an alien?
Mr. Joe: Make a straight line, kids.
Mr. Joe: Here comes your teacher!
Kids: Huh?
Daisy: Is that really Miss Gray?
Coby: Yes. Why is she wearing a diving mask and fins?
Mark: I don't know.
But she looks cool!
Daisy: She doesn't look cool.
She looks weird.
Jenna: I don't believe it.
You were right, Coby.
Jenna: She does look like an alien!
Miss Gray: Good morning, second graders.
Miss Gray: Welcome back to South Street School.
Miss Gray: Follow me, please!
Mark: Where are we going?
Coby: Swimming, I hope.
Miss Gray: We're going diving! In Room Two . . .
Miss Gray: We are going to dive into learning!
Daisy: Dive into learning?
What does that mean?
Jenna: I don't know what it means.
Jenna: But I hate to swim.
I'm probably going to drown!
Miss Gray: Please go inside and find your seat.
Mark: I sit here. Look, Coby!
You sit next to me!
Coby: Wow. Second grade is going to be great!
Jenna: I found my name.
Where are you, Daisy?
Daisy: Oh no . . . I sit way over there, next to Kara.
Daisy: She's so mean.
Daisy: I don't want to sit next to her!
Jenna: And I have to sit next to two boys.
Miss Gray: Girls, you don't look happy.
Is there a problem?
Jenna and Daisy: No, Miss Gray.
Miss Gray: Good.
Miss Gray: Okay, boys and girls, now we're going to . . .
Jenna: Our teacher is Miss Gray.
I'm having a rotten day!
Mrs. Rock: How was your first day of school, Coby?
Coby: It was great!
Mrs. Rock: Great? This morning you didn't even want to go.
Coby: I know. But now I think second grade is the best.
Mrs. Rock: Why?
Coby: Miss Gray is funny.
And I sit next to Mark.
Coby: And guess what else, Mom?
Mrs. Rock: What?
Coby: Miss Gray really likes sports.
Coby: She said she'll play basketball at recess with us.
Mrs. Rock: Oh! Well, she does sound like a fun teacher.
Jenna: Hi, Dad! Want some help?
Mr. Gibson: Sure. Gibson Laundry was very busy today.
Mr. Gibson: Mom and I worked hard all day long.
Mr. Gibson: So how was the first day of school?
Jenna: It was terrible!
Mr. Gibson: Terrible? What happened?
Jenna: I have to sit next to two boys.
Jenna: And Miss Gray is so . . .
Mr. Gibson: So what, honey?
Jenna: So strange! This morning she had on a diving mask and fins!
Jenna: Can you believe that, Dad?
Jenna: And she kept saying we're going to "dive into learning."
Mr. Gibson: Oh. Well, that sounds kind of interesting.
Customer: My son had Miss Gray.
She's a wonderful teacher, Jenna.
Jenna: Well, I still think she's strange!
Miss Gray: Yoo-hoo! I'm home!
Miss Gray: There you are!
Come on, you two.
Miss Gray: It's time to get ready.
Miss Gray: Tomorrow will be your first day of school.
Miss Gray: And I've got big plans for you!
Mark: Second grade is the best!
Jenna and Daisy: Second grade is the worst!
Mr. Joe: Good morning, boys and girls.
Mr. Joe: Miss Gray is busy with something.
Mr. Joe: So I'm going to bring you to Room Two today.
Coby: Hey, is that a maze?
Mark: I think so.
Mark: And look! There are mice!
Jenna: Did somebody say mice? Real mice?
Jim: Miss Gray, why are you wearing a stopwatch?
Miss Gray: Because Room Two is going to the races, Jim.
Class: What?
Miss Gray: Today we're diving into math.
Miss Gray: That means we're going to do a fun math activity.
Jenna: The mice won't get hurt, will they?
Miss Gray: Of course not. They're just going to race.
Miss Gray: Each mouse will run through the maze.
Miss Gray: We will time them.
Miss Gray: Then we'll use math to see which one is faster.
Mark: Mouse math!
Miss Gray: On your mark, get set . . .
Class: Go!
Miss Gray: On your mark, get set . . .
Class: Go!
Miss Gray: Let’s use mouse math now to compare them.
Mark: The black mouse took less time. So he won!
Daisy: The white mouse took twice as long.
So she lost.
Miss Gray: Good!
Jenna: They're cute.
Jenna: Do they have names?
Miss Gray: That's Jill. And this is . . . Bill.
Jenna: Hey, that rhymes!
Miss Gray: Of course. I love rhyming words.
Jenna: Miss Gray? Can I tell you something?
Miss Gray: Sure, Jenna.
Jenna: I love Room Two.
I really do!
Miss Gray: Today we're going to learn about stars.
Daisy: Yay! I love movie stars.
Rock stars too!
Miss Gray: Not those kinds of stars, Daisy.
Miss Gray: We're learning about stars in the sky.
Daisy: Oh . . .
Coby: Yes!
Mark: Twinkle, twinkle, little star . . .
Miss Gray: First, we're going to talk about stars.
Miss Gray: Then, we're going to read about them.
Miss Gray: After that, we're going to see them.
Coby: See them? How?
Miss Gray: I'll tell you more about that later.
Miss Gray: Now think for a minute.
Miss Gray: What do you know about stars?
Coby: Ooh! Ooh! Stars are big balls of hot gas!
Miss Gray: Yes . . .
Coby: And the sun is a star!
Miss Gray: Jenna, do you know anything about stars?
Jenna: Stars rhymes with bars, cars, jars.
Miss Gray: True, but we're thinking of facts about stars.
Coby: Hey! I know! Stars are—
Miss Gray: Let's give someone else a chance, Coby.
Coby: Sorry. It's just that I love stars!
Miss Gray: Okay, boys and girls.
Please sit down.
Coby: Miss Gray! Now are you going to tell us about seeing stars? Please?
Mark: Look, Coby! I'm already seeing stars!
That means I'm dizzy!
Coby: Mark! Shh!
Miss Gray: Room Two is going to see stars at the . . .
Coby: Mom! Guess what! My class is going to see stars!
Mrs. Rock: What?
Coby: We're going to the space museum!
Coby: The space museum is going to be so fun!
Coby: We're going to watch a show inside a huge globe!
Mrs. Rock: The space museum!
Coby: Here's my permission slip.
Coby: You have to sign it, or I can't go.
Mrs. Rock: I'll do that right now.
Mark: Hey, Coby! Want to play basketball?
Coby: Sure! I'll be on your team!
Mark: Okay. It's you and me against Juan and Billy.
Miss Gray: Good morning, boys and girls.
Miss Gray: Today is a big day for Room Two!
Class: Yeah!
Eve: We're going on a field trip!
We're going on a field trip!
Miss Gray: But some of you still haven't given me your permission slips.
Miss Gray: Hmm . . . Kara, Coby, and Juan.
Kara: Here's mine.
Juan: And mine.
Coby: It's in here somewhere . . .
I know my mom signed it.
Miss Gray: Coby? Do you have yours?
Mark: I'll help you look, Coby.
Jenna: Oh dear . . . I'm filled with fear.
Jenna: Did Coby lose his permission slip?
Coby: Miss Gray, I can't find it anywhere.
Miss Gray: That's too bad, Coby.
Coby: Can I still go to the space museum?
Miss Gray: Not without a signed permission slip, Coby.
Miss Gray: That's the rule at South Street.
Coby: But . . . But . . . Can we call my mom to get permission?
Miss Gray: No, Coby, I'm sorry.
Miss Gray: You'll have to stay here—in the principal's office.
Coby: Have fun at the space museum.
Mark: Sorry you can’t come with us.
Kara: That's what happens when you forget your permission slip.
Daisy: That was mean, Kara!
Kara: Sorry.
Miss Gray: Coby, bring a book with you.
And your homework.
Mr. Lenny: Hi, Coby.
Coby: Hi, Mr. Lenny.
Mr. Lenny: What are you doing here in Mr. Miller’s office?
Coby: I lost my permission slip.
Coby: So I couldn't go on the field trip.
Coby: And the space museum is my favorite place.
Mr. Lenny: Oh. That's too bad.
Coby: My class is going to see a star show and learn about planets.
Coby: And I'm stuck here, missing all the fun.
Mr. Lenny: Hmm . . . Maybe not all the fun.
Coby: What do you mean?
Mr. Lenny: I have an idea . . .
Miss Gray: Room Two, please take a seat.
Miss Gray: The star show starts in three minutes.
Mark: Cool! The ceiling is shaped like a globe.
Miss Gray: That's right.
Miss Gray: The ceiling is supposed to look like the night sky.
Miss Gray: Shh, everyone!
Kids: Ooh! Whoa . . .
Mark: Look! There's the Milky Way! And Saturn!
Mark: Too bad Coby missed the star show.
Jenna: I know. Poor Coby.
Jenna: He's probably so bored right now.
Mark: Yep.
Mr. Lenny: Ready, helper?
Coby: I'm ready, Mr. Lenny!
Mr. Lenny: Then let's go.
Mr. Lenny: Our first job is to fix the slide on the playground . . .
Mr. Lenny: We're going to tighten some bolts.
Coby: Hey . . . What's Mr. Miller doing?
Mr. Lenny: He's telling Mandy to take her dog home.
Mr. Lenny: No dogs allowed at school.
Coby: What's our next job, Mr. Lenny?
Mr. Lenny: We have to sweep the art room floor.
Coby: Okay. This is fun!
Coby: Look! Now Mr. Miller is visiting kindergarten.
Mr. Miller: That's it for me, kids.
I'm exhausted.
Coby: Wow, the principal has a hard job!
Miss Gray: Who knows what planet this is?
Mark: Coby would know if he were here.
Daisy: It's red, so I think it's Mars.
Miss Gray: Right, Daisy. Mars is called the red planet.
Miss Gray: On Mars the sky looks pink.
Kara: Pink! That's my favorite color!
Mark: Where are we going next?
Miss Gray: The gift shop.
Mark: Oh good. I brought money to buy something.
Mr. Lenny: This is our last job—cleaning the principal's windows.
Mr. Lenny: Oh . . . That's odd.
Coby: Yeah. Why are the lights off?
Coby: Wow! This is amazing!
Mr. Miller: It's been a hard day.
So I'm relaxing under the stars.
Mr. Miller: But don't tell anyone!
Coby: It's awesome! I can see the Big Dipper!
Mark: Coby! We're back.
Sorry you missed the star show. But look.
Mark: I brought you something from the gift shop.
Mark: Was it really boring here?
Coby: Umm . . . Well, I did get to be Mr. Lenny's helper.
Coby: And that was fun!
Daisy: Miss Gray, is Picture Day coming soon?
Miss Gray: Yes. It's next week, Daisy.
Daisy: Finally!
Mark: Who cares about Picture Day?
Daisy: Me! I love Picture Day.
Mark: Why? All we do is stand there and smile at the camera.
Coby: Yeah. It's sooo boring!
Daisy: Well, I want to be a rock star one day. Or a dancer.
Daisy: So I like to get my picture taken.
Kara: I like Picture Day too, Daisy.
Daisy: Oh.
Kara: Because my mom always buys me a pretty new dress.
Coby: My mom gets me a new dress too!
Mark: Ha-ha! Come on, Coby.
Mark: Let's practice getting our picture taken!
Coby and Mark: Cheese!
Daisy: Very funny, you two.
Daisy: Just don't make those silly faces on the real Picture Day.
Jenna: Yeah! That will ruin our class picture.
Daisy: Guess what, Mom! Picture Day is coming soon.
Mrs. Gomez: Oh, good. We'll have new pictures to send to your grandparents.
Daisy: Can I get a new dress? Please?
Mrs. Gomez: I'm sorry, Daisy.
A new dress costs too much.
Daisy: Oh . . . That's okay . . .
Mrs. Gomez: But we can borrow your cousin's blue dress.
Mrs. Gomez: And we'll get new ribbons for your hair too.
Daisy: Great idea, Mom.
I'll be so beautiful, I won't need a new dress!
Mrs. Gomez: Right!
Jenna: Daisy, I like your dress.
Daisy: Thank you. I borrowed it from my cousin.
Jenna: I have on my favorite shirt for Picture Day.
Daisy: Yay! The purple one!
Jenna: You look nice, Mark.
Mark: Thanks. I'm wearing my monster tie.
Mark: It makes me walk like a monster!
Jenna and Daisy: Ah!
Jenna: Ugh. Look who's coming.
Daisy: Oh no. It's Kara.
Daisy: She's going to show off her new clothes.
Kara: Hi, Daisy! Hi, Jenna!
Kara: Do you notice anything different about me?
Daisy: Um . . . No.
Jenna: Me neither.
Jenna: Come on, Daisy. Let's go line up.
Miss Gray: We're getting our pictures taken soon.
Miss Gray: But first we have a treat.
Mark: Yes! A treat!
Jim: What is it?
Coby: Please, oh please. Let it be an extra recess.
Miss Gray: Sorry, Coby. It's not an extra recess.
Miss Gray: But it's something good—today is Maya's birthday.
Maya: Yep. It's my birthday.
Maya: So I brought in muffins and juice for everyone.
Class: Happy Birthday, Maya!
Maya: Thank you. Mark? Can you please help me give out the treats?
Mark: Sure. Monster Mark is at your service.
Jim: Yum. Berry juice!
Daisy: Thanks for the muffin, Maya.
Mark: One berry juice coming right up, Daisy. Whoops!
Daisy: Oh no! Mark!
Mark: I'm so sorry, Daisy!
Daisy: My dress! My cousin is going to be so mad at me!
Miss Gray: I'm sorry that happened, Daisy.
Miss Gray: Mark, you should not have been walking like a monster!
Mark: I know. I'm sorry.
Miss Gray: The school nurse will help you get cleaned up.
Miss Gray: Maybe your mom can bring you some new clothes.
Daisy: She's working today.
Miss Gray: Well, the nurse will have dry clothes for you.
Daisy: But . . . But . . . It's Picture Day.
Miss Gray: I know, honey. It's a shame.
School Nurse: Here you go, Daisy.
These clothes should fit you.
Daisy: Thank you.
Jenna: You still look pretty, Daisy.
Daisy: No, I don't.
I don't like orange and I don't like teddy bears.
Daisy: Why, oh why, did this have to happen today?
Photographer: Miss Gray's class, you're next!
Mark: Don't worry, Daisy.
Mark: Coby and I won't make any silly faces. We promise.
Coby: Yeah. Our class picture is going to be great!
Kara: Yuck. Didn't the nurse have any nice clothes?
Daisy: No.
Photographer: On the count of three, everybody say "Cheese!"
Photographer: One . . . Two . . .
Kara: You're going to ruin the picture.
Daisy: No, I'm not! I can't help it if—
Photographer: Three!
Class: Cheese!
Miss Gray: Our pictures are here, class.
Daisy: Uh-oh.
Mark: How does our class picture look?
Miss Gray: Um . . .
Coby: Oh boy.
Maya: Not good.
Eve: I really wanted a nice class picture.
Jim: Me too.
Daisy: It's my fault. And Kara's.
Kara: I didn't do anything.
Daisy: Yes, you did. You were saying mean things to me!
Kara: Well, you should blame Mark, not me.
Kara: He's the one who spilled juice on you!
Miss Gray: Okay, girls, that's enough.
Miss Gray: Class, please put the pictures away.
Miss Gray: It's time to go home.
Daisy: Your dad is the best at cleaning clothes, Jenna.
Jenna: That's why he owns a laundry business, I guess.
Jenna: I'm glad all the juice stains came out.
Daisy: Me too.
Jenna: But why did Miss Gray tell us to wear our Picture Day clothes again?
Daisy: I don't know.
Daisy: Look! Monster Mark is back.
Daisy: Ah! Don't come near me!
Miss Gray: I have good news, class.
Miss Gray: It's Picture Day again.
Class: What?
Daisy: What do you mean, Miss Gray?
Miss Gray: The photographer is coming back at ten o'clock.
Miss Gray: He's going to take our picture again.
Miss Gray: Maybe this one will come out better.
Class: Hooray!
Daisy: I won't make a mean face this time.
Kara: Me neither.
Photographer: Okay, Room Two.
Photographer: On the count of three, say "Cheese."
Photographer: One . . . Two . . . Three!
Class: Cheese!
Miss Gray: The school science fair is next month.
Miss Gray: And you know how I feel about science!
Jenna: How, Miss Gray?
Miss Gray: I love it!
Mark: Why do you love science?
Miss Gray: Because it helps us learn about plants and—
Coby: Space!
Jenna: And weather!
Juan: And animals!
Miss Gray: Right! Science is about all of those things.
Miss Gray: And I know everyone in this class will make great projects.
Mark: Coby, what's your science fair project?
Coby: I'm going to count stars in the night sky.
Mark: That's a good idea.
Kara: I'm studying caterpillars.
Mark: What about them?
Kara: How they turn into beautiful butterflies.
Jenna: I'm making a tornado in a bottle.
Maya: Me too!
Daisy: Hey! I'm doing the same project!
Coby: What's your science project, Mark?
Mark: I haven't thought of one yet.
Coby: You're good at science.
I'll bet you'll think of something cool.
Maya: You could make soap bubbles.
Mark: Nah. Bubbles are for babies.
Coby: You could study evaporation.
Mark: Boring!
Jenna: Why don't you ask Miss Gray?
She's got lots of good ideas.
Mark: I know. But I want to surprise her with a really cool project.
Kara: You'd better think of something soon, Mark.
Kara: It takes a long time to make a good project.
Coby: Did you think of an idea for the science fair yet?
Mark: Yep. I'm going to watch a plant.
To see how it grows.
Coby: You're going to watch a plant?
Mark: It'll be cool.
Coby: It sounds . . . um . . . boring.
Mark: Really?
Coby: Yeah. But I'm glad you're not making a tornado in a bottle.
Coby: Everybody is making those!
Mark: Come on, plant.
Don't just sit there. Grow!
Zack: You look weird.
What are you doing?
Mark: I'm working on my science project.
Mark: It was fun when the seed sprouted.
Mark: But now it's—
Zack: Boring!
Juan: Hi, Mark. Want to come out and play football?
Mark: I can't. I'm working on my project.
Mark: I'm watching a plant grow.
Juan: Oh. That sounds . . . uh . . . fun! Bye.
Mark: Coby and Zack were right.
This project is boring!
Mark: Hey, guys! Can I play football?
Coby: When are we going to share our science projects?
Miss Gray: The fair is still weeks away, Coby.
Miss Gray: We'll share them on the day of the fair.
Maya and Jenna: I can't wait!
Kara: My project is sooo great!
Kara: I'm going to win a ribbon for sure!
Miss Gray: I'm sure everyone will have a great project.
Miss Gray: I'm looking forward to . . .
Miss Gray: Mark? What's wrong?
Mark: I have a problem—a science fair problem!
Miss Gray: Let's go into the hall, Mark.
Miss Gray: Please tell me what's wrong.
Mark: I'm doing my science project on how a plant grows.
Mark: But watching a plant is boring—really boring!
Mark: And now I don't know what to do.
Miss Gray: You could choose a new project.
Mark: I guess I could do that . . .
Miss Gray: You always have good ideas, Mark.
Miss Gray: I'm sure you'll think of something wonderful.
Mrs. Conlan: Are you doing your homework?
Mark: I'm thinking of ideas for a new science project.
Zack: What happened to the plant project?
Mark: You were right.
It was boring.
Zack: Why don't you make a tornado in a bottle?
Zack: They're really cool.
You shake them and—
Mark: Yeah, yeah, I know.
Everybody is making those.
Mark: I like plants.
So I want to have a plant project.
Mark: But it has to be something cool.
Mrs. Conlan: Hmm . . .
Mr. Conlan: Zack! Are you ready? Come on.
Mr. Conlan: It's time for your basketball game!
Zack: Oh no. He's got his cameras again.
Mrs. Conlan: You boys are growing up so fast.
Mrs. Conlan: Your father loves taking pictures of you.
Mark: That's it! I've got a great idea!
Mrs. Conlan: Where are you going, Mark?
Mark: Hey, Dad! When you get back, can I borrow your video camera?
Kara: Hi, Mark! Hi, Coby!
Kara: Want to see my project again?
It's about butterflies.
Mark and Coby: No, thanks.
Mark: Wow! Are those raisins?
Juan: Yes. I mixed vinegar with baking soda to make them swim.
Coby: Cool!
Mrs. Conlan: Mark, the judges are going to your table.
Mrs. Conlan: You'd better get over there.
Mark: The best projects win ribbons.
Mark: I hope I win one!
Judge 1: What's your project, young man?
Mark: I studied how plants grow.
Mark: And I made a movie about it.
Judge 2: You made a movie?
May we see it?
Mark: Sure!
Judge 1: Hmm.
Judge 2: Oh . . .
Judge 1: Your project is very unusual. Thank you.
Zack: Now what?
Mrs. Conlan: We have to wait for the judges to decide.
Mr. Conlan: Mark, let me take another picture of you.
Mr. Conlan: Stand right there, in front of your plant again!
Mrs. Conlan: What are those?
Mark: Tornados in a bottle.
Mr. Conlan: I see they were popular this year.
Mark: That's for sure.
Mr. Miller: Thank you for coming to the science fair.
Mr. Miller: We had some great projects this year.
Mr. Miller: Soon we'll be giving out ribbons for the best ones.
Mark: I hope mine wins.
Mr. Miller: But first, we'd like to show you a project.
Man: Show us? What is he talking about?
Mr. Miller: Lights, please!
Crowd: Amazing! Wow!
Miss Gray: Nice job, Mark!
You won a ribbon!
Mark: Thanks, Miss Gray.
Miss Gray: I just love science, don't you?
Mark: Yes!
Mr. Miller: Good morning, Room Two!
Class: Good morning, Mr. Miller!
Mr. Miller: I'm here to tell you about the Superstar Reading Contest.
Juan: What's that?
Miss Gray: Shh.
Mr. Miller: I'm asking Room Two to read, read, read!
Jim: I don't like to read.
Jenna: You don't like to read?
I love to read.
Miss Gray: Jim. Jenna. Please listen.
Mr. Miller: Room Two must read one hundred books this month.
Mr. Miller: If you do, I'll celebrate by doing something wacky.
Mark: Like what, Mr. Miller?
Mr. Miller: I'll shave off all my hair!
Coby: But you're bald!
Kids: Ha-ha!
Mr. Miller: I'll surprise you with something wacky, I promise.
Kids: Woo-hoo! Hooray!
Jenna: No problem, Mr. Miller.
We can do it!
Jenna: Dad, can you take me to the library?
Mr. Gibson: Sure. What for?
Jenna: Mr. Miller wants our class to read one hundred books.
Jenna: If we do, he'll do something wacky.
Mr. Gibson: That sounds like a big challenge.
Jenna: Nope. I can probably read one hundred books all by myself.
Mr. Gibson: You do love to read!
Mrs. Gibson: Did you find good books at the library?
Jenna: Yes!
Mrs. Gibson: Wow. But they're all thick chapter books, honey.
Mrs. Gibson: Are you sure you can read them in a month?
Jenna: Yep, I'm sure.
When it comes to reading, I'm already a superstar!
Coby: Do we have any homework?
Mark: It's Friday. And we don't get homework on weekends.
Mark: Right, Miss Gray?
Miss Gray: Actually, Mark, I am giving you homework this weekend.
Class: Oh no.
Miss Gray: Everyone has to read, read, read!
Mark: Oh, right, the Superstar Reading Contest.
Coby: Don't worry, Miss Gray.
We can do it.
Coby: And we have Jenna in our class.
Class: Yay, Jenna!
Mrs. Gibson: You've got a busy day, Jenna.
Mrs. Gibson: Your soccer game is at ten.
Mrs. Gibson: And Ella's pool party starts at three.
Jenna: Mmm-hmm . . .
Coach: Jenna!
Jenna: Sorry. We're having a reading contest at school.
Jenna: And I'm still reading my first book.
Coach: Well, the game starts in two minutes.
Mr. Gibson: Shoot, Jenna!
Mrs. Gibson: Good try, honey!
Coach: Come on, girls! Play hard out there!
Mrs. Gibson: Jenna's running a lot today.
Mr. Gibson: Two players are sick today.
Mr. Gibson: So the other girls have to play extra hard.
Mrs. Gibson: Happy Birthday, Ella.
Ella: Thanks, Mrs. Gibson.
Come in the pool, Jenna!
Mrs. Gibson: Remember the rules, Jenna.
No reading in the pool!
Daisy: Ella's pool party was fun, wasn't it?
Jenna: Yeah. The best part was the slide.
Daisy: I know. We went down it about fifty times!
Mr. Gibson: Where's Jenna?
Mrs. Gibson: In her room, reading.
Mr. Gibson: Wow . . . I bet our reading superstar [n3@is on her third or fourth book by now.
Kids: Hi, Mr. Miller.
Mr. Miller: Hi, kids. Is it time for recess?
Daisy: Yes. Do you know what our reading prize is yet?
Coby: Remember, Mr. Miller, you promised to do something wacky!
Mr. Miller: Only if Room Two reads one hundred books.
Daisy: We will. We have Jenna in our class!
Coby: Do you know what you're going to do yet?
Mr. Miller: I have a few ideas.
Mr. Miller: I might let someone throw a pie in my face.
Mark: Ooh! Can I do it?
Daisy: What are your other ideas?
Mr. Miller: I might dance on the school roof.
Mr. Miller: Or eat some worms.
Kara: Yuck!
Mr. Miller: Whatever it is, it will be wacky.
I promise. Bye, kids.
Mark: I can't wait to see what he does.
Coby: It's going to be great.
